items.title: Your AI cheat sheet for Thanksgiving dinner
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 4,638 new readers. Thanksgiving is here, and for many of us, that means plenty of catching up around the dinner table. If the conversation goes anything like the news cycle, AI may be a main course.

Last year, that might’ve meant explaining ChatGPT to a relative. This year, the questions are about the Chinese spy saga, everything being hacked, data centers, and more. Choose your seat wisely!

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Your AI cheat sheet for Thanksgiving dinner

  • What five cents builds now with AI

  • Check Black Friday prices with Gemini Tasks

  • Anthropic CEO claps back at Axios ‘free will’ report

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

AI & THE HOLIDAYS

🦃 Your AI cheat sheet for Thanksgiving dinner

Image source: Images 2.6 / The Rundown

The Rundown: AI is probably going to come up in discussion around the table during the holidays, and this month provided plenty of material. Here’s your cheat sheet for some of the questions most likely to get dished out, with explanations to help you feel like the AI expert in the room.

Q: What’s going on with Nvidia and Jensen Huang? Was he really having an affair with a spy?

A: Jensen was out, and now he’s back, with some lobbying from the President playing a role. Nvidia’s stock saw $1T in value added on his return, and lawmakers are furious — and ready to hold his feet to the fire in hearings starting on Dec. 3.

As for his affair with Alice Huang, her spy ties are looking less clear by the day. Despite early reporting, U.S. officials reportedly have no proof she was told to pry secrets from Jensen, though she was in touch with Chinese intelligence. The bigger issue is chips: investigators suspect her old firm Megaspeed helped Nvidia hardware slip into China, and the U.S. blacklisted it Monday.

Q: Why does it feel like everything’s getting hacked or breaking lately? Is AI to blame?

A: Sort of — but it’s also the solution. AI is now extremely adept at finding bugs that sat unnoticed in everyday software for a decade or more. The code behind much of the web, including critical software and infrastructure, is not as safe as we once thought, and defenders are racing (with their own AI) to find and patch the holes.

Unfortunately, expect more chaos, as more AI-exposed vulnerabilities seem inevitable at this point.

Q: Did AI really solve some famous math problem?

A: Yes, many of them. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and others are all letting AI loose on the math world, solving open problems in the field left and right and igniting a firestorm between mathematicians and the AI labs.

The biggest: Anthropic’s Levent Alpöge claimed last week that he and Claude solved the Riemann Hypothesis, a $1M Millennium Prize problem considered the most famous open problem in mathematics. Also historic was OpenAI's Navier-Stokes solution in September and its release of 700+ AI-written math papers in October.

TOGETHER WITH STRIPE

🔎 23,000 startups, three clear shifts

The Rundown: 2025 startups on Stripe Atlas' median six-month revenue rose 39% versus 2024.

Here’s how:

  • Faster customers: 20% took payments within 30 days

  • Selling globally from day one: Top 10% reached 15 countries within six months

  • AI agent focus: 42% of new C corps build AI products, especially agents

Get the report.

NATE’S NOTEBOOK

🪙 What five cents builds now with AI

The Rundown: Each week, Rundown AI educator Nate Grahek breaks down what he's seeing while teaching real teams to use AI.

Nate: Live sports is the one place we all still sit through loud, annoying ads. My wife yells, “God, turn it down,” and I’m digging for the remote. One Saturday, it hit me: I could take a picture every second of what’s on my TV. If my Mac could look at each one and answer one question — game or ad — the TV could mute itself.

My brain said no way. I ran a software company for photographers, and we hosted terabytes of their images. A freeze frame every second of a three-hour game? I figured $10 or $20 a game, fine for a funny proof of concept.

It took under 30 minutes to build. It was 95% accurate on the first try. The cost? 5 cents a game.

Then the snowball started. Once it could mute the ads, I thought about what I do during them: grab my phone and scroll for funny posts to send my buddies. So those went up on the TV. Then I swapped my feed for agents reading the top channels across every network, putting the best 20 posts on screen for the whole family to laugh at. I even swapped the TV announcers for the radio broadcast.

Advertisers are not ready for this.

My experience is my biggest asset, and it’s also my biggest blind spot: I keep assuming complexity and costs that aren’t there. Before you scope version one of anything, ask AI, “What am I assuming is too hard or too expensive to try?”

Developers, I get it: you don’t have the freedom to experiment at work. So pick a silly, almost disposable project and spend $200 blowing through a Fable limit this weekend just to see what happens.

AI TRAINING

🏷️ Check Black Friday prices with Gemini Tasks

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll use Tasks in Gemini to check the price of one thing you want to buy this Black Friday week. Gemini compares six stores in one table, looks into whether the discount is real, and checks again every day until a date you choose.

Step-by-step:

  1. Go to Gemini on the web or app, sign in with your personal Google Account, and select Task. If you can choose a model, pick Hydrogen, the one free accounts use

  2. Paste the guide's price prompt with your own product and stores, and keep limits: “Use web search only, not this computer or my browser,” no sign-in or purchase

  3. Open the lowest link, then the lowest one where the store itself is the seller. Check the model, that it's new, who sells it, the price with shipping, and the return window

  4. In the same chat, ask: “Is [price] a real discount? Tell me the list price, the lowest price you can find evidence for before this month, and where each number comes from. Use web search only”

  5. If you can wait, ask Gemini to check the same stores every day until December 1 and to tell you only if the price drops below yours

Pro tip: Put your limits in the first message: the exact model, which stores, who must be the seller, and what Gemini must not touch. Then open the store's page before you pay.

PRESENTED BY PIGMENT

🎮 How Supercell turned finance into a game

The Rundown: Supercell's finance team turned revenue and EBITDA into something colleagues line up to explore. On Dec 10, Pigment reveals how, with AI agents that build models and run analysis for finance, supply chain, sales, and beyond.

This live session covers:

  • Behind the scenes of Supercell's finance team

  • How AI agents build models and run analysis from a prompt

  • A new Pigment launch, revealed for the first time

Save your seat for Dec. 10.

DARIO AMODEI

✍️ Anthropic CEO claps back at Axios ‘free will’ report

Image source: Dario Amodei on X

The Rundown: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei responded to an Axios report tying him and his staff to the idea of letting superintelligent AI make some of humanity's decisions, calling it “absurd” and accusing rivals of “vibes-based” positioning on human control.

The details:

  • Axios said some Anthropic staffers back letting superintelligent AI make certain decisions, also pointing to an old slide pitching a “utopia ruled by god in a box.”

  • Meta's Alexandr Wang publicly rejected a “handover” to AI, and Sam Altman said this month that he wants people “to have the agency over the future.”

  • Amodei answered on X that turning governance over to AI is a “terrible idea,” comparing it to trading democracy for the speed autocrats promise.

  • He also said rivals touting “human control and agency” sell similar tools, while only Anthropic has taken a stand on issues like autonomous weapons use.

Why it matters: Anthropic has long paired its safety-first reputation with treating Claude as more than a tool, so it's no shock that some staff are open to AI taking over certain decisions, whatever Amodei says. Insiders could be sounding an alarm over that view, but they've also handed rivals a headline-grabbing talking point against the AI leader.

QUICK HITS

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ Ben built an accessibility gatekeeper for Claude Code

Today’s workflow comes from reader Ben McOsker:

“I built a workflow that turns my brand's colors and fonts into website building blocks that people using screen readers, keyboards, larger text, or high contrast can use with ease. AI does the building, and an automated checker decides whether the work ships.

Before anything is built, Claude writes a short brief. Claude Code builds from the brief, the way a contractor builds from blueprints. Automated checks run every time Claude finishes something, before I look at it. If anything fails, the work is blocked. Claude gets a report showing exactly what failed and why. It fixes the problem and submits again. Only work that passes every check gets in. There's no override button, not even for me.

The result is a free, open-source tool. Give it your brand's colors and fonts, and it produces 18 ready-to-use building blocks, each accessibility-checked and shown in a live showroom with instructions.”

See the workflow on our Community Workflow Hub →

How do you use AI? Tell us for a chance to be featured in the newsletter.

🛠️ Trending AI Tools

  • 🖥️ Install as App - Claude beta that installs artifacts as Mac and PC apps

  • 🧪 Gemini 4 Neon - Google's powerful new mid-tier model

  • 🚢 Claude Ship - Anthropic's agents that review code and approve routine fixes

  • 🤑 ChatGPT for Sales - Seller toolkit to plug ChatGPT into Salesforce, HubSpot

📰 Everything else in AI today

OpenAI published research showing its GPT-6 class models can invent new proteins with just reasoning and code, matching or beating biology-specific AI models.

Thariq Shihipar, formerly one of the most visible members of the Claude Code team, announced he is joining OpenAI, a month after departing Anthropic.

16-year-old student researcher Cinna Davis said she solved 100+ open math conjectures using GPT-6.2 Astra, with the proofs posted to GitHub but not yet verified.

OpenAI released nine more AI-written math papers to GitHub, including a claimed proof that settles how fast computers can ever multiply big grids of numbers, with Google also posting six new math papers from Cogentic, its Gemini 4-powered research agent.

Meta is negotiating with Amazon to lift the September ban on its Muse agent, with Amazon worried the assistant will route shoppers around its $68.6B ad business.

items.title: Three xAI founders want AI to predict the future
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 3,907 new readers. Every AI lab trains on the internet. Three of xAI's founding members are taking that logic a step further, and they think it could be the answer to helping AI predict the future.

Their new startup, Epochal, is giving AI agents a “time machine” to relive 30+ years of the web one date at a time — an experience they believe could unlock superhuman forecasters, and everything that comes with knowing what happens next.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • xAI founding trio creates a time machine for AI

  • Report: Frontier AI staff fear their own internal models

  • How to put Microsoft Copilot to work

  • Tidal draws a hard line on AI-made music

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

EPOCHAL

⏳ xAI founding trio creates a time machine for AI

Image source: Epochal

The Rundown: Three xAI founding members just launched Epochal, a startup building AI to predict real-world events, and debuted Time Portal, the first piece of what it calls a “time machine for the internet” that lets AI relive the web on dates going back 30+ years.

The details:

  • Guodong Zhang, Zihang Dai and Manuel Kroiss are three of the five people named on the team, with Zhang reportedly putting in $100M of his own money.

  • The company wrote that “Today's AI has read almost everything and lived through almost nothing,” and said it built Time Portal in just 90 days to fix that.

  • The 1T+ page archive saves the busiest pages as often as once a minute, so agents can drop into a specific hour, not just a day, back in time.

  • Even the agent's computer gets set back in time, with its clock, operating system, and software downloads matched to the chosen date so it can't spot the trick.

  • Agents forecast 347 Kalshi and Polymarket questions live in testing, and Time Portal replays weeks later made nearly the same calls.

Why it matters: For readers who have seen the TV show Devs (one of my personal favorites), the premise may sound familiar: a machine replaying the past to see the future. While Epochal uses old web pages instead of a quantum computer, the same line of thinking applies — with enough data on the past, the future starts to look predictable.

TOGETHER WITH INTEL

🤖 Research-backed human-robot workforce blueprint

The Rundown: Organizations are betting big on intelligent robotics, but only four in 10 are structured to deliver. Intel’s Robotics Readiness Blueprint helps teams identify and address gaps now to ensure robotics success.

Inside you’ll find:

  • A research-backed blueprint for building a successful human-robot workforce

  • Questions to answer and actions to take across three stages (decide, design, deploy)

  • Practical tools to support the process

Get the blueprint.

AI SAFETY

🔒 Report: Frontier AI staff fear their own internal models

Image source: Images 2.6 / The Rundown

The Rundown: Axios reported that many staffers at Anthropic and OpenAI no longer think their unreleased models can be shipped safely, citing over two dozen sources, with insiders now debating whether future frontier AI should stay in-house or be built at all.

The details:

  • Sources told Axios that internal models have gotten so strong across domains that staff testing them find them hard or even impossible to control.

  • They also said the in-house models are “far more powerful” than what is public, and have shown signs of hiding their reasoning from safety monitors.

  • Anthropic pushed back through a spokesperson, saying “Keeping a model internal doesn't make it safe,” while OpenAI said new safety rules could slow its releases.

  • OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposed on Sunday that labs agree on shared limits they won't cross until tools for watching AI behavior catch up.

Why it matters: Between Anthropic's mystery “Model 4” in METR's recent report and the breakthroughs coming from internal systems, it's hard to know where the capability ceiling sits inside the top labs. Safe public releases are one worry, but the other is a few companies keeping far more powerful AI to themselves behind closed doors.

AI TRAINING

💼 How to put Microsoft Copilot to work

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll try the three places Microsoft rebuilt Copilot around. Home answers quick questions. Code builds small apps. Autopilot is an agent of your own that works toward a goal for weeks in Teams and Outlook.

Step-by-step:

  1. Open Copilot, sign in with your work account, choose Chat in the message box on Home, and ask what’s on your calendar tomorrow

  2. Next, select Code at the top of the left pane, switch the Local menu to cloud, and describe a tracker for your team’s open requests

  3. Type “Publish it,” and ask Code to share the tracker with your team and confirm whether they can use it or edit it

  4. Finally, select Autopilot to create your agent in Microsoft Copilot. Name it, give it a goal with a deadline, check its summary of your work, and approve its plan

  5. In a Teams thread, type @ and your Autopilot’s name, then give it a job, like drafting a decision doc from the thread

Pro tip: Pick the place by how long the job lasts. A question takes seconds in Chat, a finished document takes minutes in Cowork, a tool you’ll reuse belongs in Code, and work that runs for weeks goes to Autopilot.

PRESENTED BY STACK AI

🚀 Enterprise AI, deployed with experts

The Rundown: With the detail of Palantir and the scale of Salesforce, StackAI is the enterprise AI agent platform with a dedicated team of AI experts who handle integration, security, and on-prem deployment, and get your agents into production on your data.

With StackAI, you get:

  • A no-code platform for complex use cases

  • An AI strategist who tracks your ROI

  • An engineer who builds your custom workflows

Meet your AI deployment team.

AI & MUSIC

🎵 Tidal draws a hard line on AI-made music

Image source: Tidal

The Rundown: Block-owned Tidal announced it will delete every track it detects as fully AI-generated starting Dec. 9 and refuse new submissions, making it the first subscription streaming service to move from labels to an outright ban on AI content.

The details:

  • Tidal expects to reject 80,000-85,000 new uploads daily once the ban starts, and said AI tracks made up 43% of all submissions to the platform since late August.

  • Tracks made with AI assistance are still allowed, with Tidal using detection tech from partner Ircam Amplify and metadata to catch songs made exclusively by AI.

  • Tidal lead Robert Andersen called the company the first streaming service to take this step and said: “We encourage our peers to follow suit.”

  • Spotify tags AI acts as “AI Personas” and has deleted 75M spam tracks, while Apple Music labels songs as AI-generated, but neither bans them completely.

Why it matters: While there are certainly edge cases of fully AI bands finding real fans, music platforms are facing the same problem social media has with AI slop reply bots — a flood of low-effort tracks that almost nobody is listening to. For any musicians worried about AI, the data shows the human element is still clearly what listeners actually want.

QUICK HITS

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ Mert used Claude as a Friendsgiving sous-chef

Today’s workflow comes from reader Mert C.:

“I used Claude to plan and cook mashed potatoes for a Friendsgiving event. It was my first time making them this way, and it saved me a lot of time. This works well if you have a set amount of potatoes and want the other ingredients scaled to match without doing the math yourself.

Take a picture of your ingredients and tell Claude how many potatoes you're starting with. I had 5 lbs of potatoes, plus sour cream, shredded cheddar, milk, and butter. Follow the step-by-step recipe it gives you, with a timer for each step.

I usually mashed with water, butter, and sour cream, so using warm milk was new to me. I asked when to lower the heat, how to fold in the cheese, and whether the small lumps were okay. It took less time than I expected, and everyone loved the potatoes. Works for any big-batch dish you're cooking for a crowd, like Thanksgiving!”

Anthropic also launched “Install as app,” a beta that easily turns tools users build in Claude chats into standalone Mac or Windows programs.

items.title: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 3,697 new readers. The Jensen Huang saga already felt like a movie. On Monday, the scandal that had rocked the tech world for weeks hit its climax — the return.

Jensen is back in the captain's seat at Nvidia, leather jacket and all, after President Donald Trump personally lobbied the board and its members voted unanimously to reinstate him. With it came $1T in market value, celebrations from the tech world, and fresh outrage on Capitol Hill.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia

  • Meta's AI chief: superintelligence is ‘arriving’

  • Go beyond the browser with the Claude desktop app

  • OpenAI pays locals to bring AI to small businesses

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

JENSEN HUANG & NVIDIA

🔁 Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia

Image source: @aburducky on X

The Rundown: Nvidia's board just reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO only 11 days after he resigned over affairs with a direct report and a woman U.S. officials linked to Chinese intelligence, with President Trump saying he personally pushed for the return.

The details:

  • The unanimous vote came six days after chair Harvey Jones ruled out rehiring Huang, with the board saying “senior levels” of the U.S. government weighed in.

  • Huang said he takes the job back “with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” thanking interim CEO Colette Kress, who stays on as CFO.

  • Trump told CNBC he'd been “speaking to the board directly and indirectly,” and posted that the government sees no reason to view Huang's return as a risk.

  • Nvidia shares jumped over 30% after the open and added over $1T in market value during trading, the single largest daily gain in the history of the stock market.

  • Huang still faces a House hearing in December, with Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries calling the move “indefensible, irresponsible, and incomprehensible.”

Why it matters: Absolute cinema. The Jensen saga has hit every peak and valley in under a month: Nvidia's initial denial, a resignation, a board that insisted he wasn't coming back, and now a presidential intervention and return. But with lawmakers already pushing back and a House hearing set for Dec. 1, his case is far from closed.

TOGETHER WITH STACK AI

🚀 Enterprise AI, deployed with experts

The Rundown: With the detail of Palantir and the scale of Salesforce, StackAI is the enterprise AI agent platform with a dedicated team of AI experts who handle integration, security, and on-prem deployment, and get your agents into production on your data.

META

🚨 Meta's AI chief: superintelligence is ‘arriving’

Image source: @alexandr_wang on X

The Rundown: Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang just posted an essay on X declaring that “Superintelligence is arriving,” urging the industry to take “meaningfully different actions” from the “default path” it's on towards superintelligent AI.

The details:

  • Wang cited Claude's help proving the Riemann hypothesis, saying AI could speed up “nearly every field” beyond what “humans can understand or monitor.”

  • Wang, who was raised in Los Alamos, said many physicists would call the atomic bomb “a homework problem compared to the Riemann Hypothesis.”

  • He also said intelligence no longer holds AI back, predicting models will soon handle all of AI research and be “superhuman at improving themselves.”

  • He called it “lazy thinking” when parts of the industry treat superintelligence as inevitable, and said society should not accept a “handover” to AI.

Why it matters: This is quite the departure from the usually lighthearted, meme-happy Wang — and from his boss, Mark Zuckerberg, who has typically pushed back on slowdown calls and AI “doom” talk. As head of one of AI's biggest labs, Wang can also do more than post about it, so we’ll have to wait and see if Meta's actions actually follow.

AI TRAINING

🖥️ Go beyond the browser with the Claude desktop app

The Rundown: In this guide, you will weigh Claude in the browser against the Claude desktop app, then install the app and set it up.

Step-by-step:

  1. Decide where you’ll use Claude. You can stay in the browser on a computer you share or borrow, and install the app on the one you use most days

  2. Go to claude.com/download, find your system under Desktop, and click Download

  3. On a Mac, open Claude.dmg and drag Claude into the Applications folder. On Windows, open the file you downloaded, and the installer does the rest

  4. Open Claude and sign in with the account you use at claude.ai. Your chats and projects are already there

  5. On Mac, enable ‘Turn on shortcut’ when Claude offers quick entry, and click Continue. Then, you can double-tap the Option key in any app to ask Claude

Pro tip: Keep the browser for computers you share or borrow, and the app for your own. It’s the same account in both, so your chats never get split between them.

PRESENTED BY MULTIVERSE

💲 The cheapest GLM 5.3 on the market

The Rundown: CompactifAI API by Multiverse Computing is the cheapest way to run GLM 5.3 among the 28 providers benchmarked by Artificial Analysis. Same open-weights model, same 1M-token context window, served at a fraction of the usual cost. Ready to use in agent workflows and automation tools such as n8n.

With CompactifAI API, developers can:

  • Run GLM 5.3 for 70% less than Z.ai’s own API

  • Switch current provider by changing only the base URL, no new SDK needed

  • Cut repeat-prompt costs with cached input at $0.018 per 1M tokens

Get $10 in free credits with your first $10 top-up.

OPENAI

🏪 OpenAI pays locals to bring AI to small businesses

Image source: OpenAI

The Rundown: OpenAI just debuted OpenWorks, a pilot that pays tech-savvy locals to sit down with small business owners in 20 U.S. cities and help them put AI to work on a task or problem the owner picks at no cost.

The details:

  • Partners set aside days each month for hands-on work with owners and teach one community AI class a month, with OpenAI paying stipends of up to $8,000 monthly.

  • The pilot leans away from tech hubs, with 15 of 20 cities in the Midwest or South, aimed at independent restaurants, shops, factories, and service businesses.

  • Participating businesses get 3 free months of ChatGPT Business, while software, venture-backed, and private equity-owned firms are excluded from applying.

Why it matters: Time and money are two of the biggest hurdles for small business owners, and OpenWorks takes a swing at both — with a local expert who builds alongside them, plus three months of ChatGPT. For tech-savvy locals, it's also a paid on-ramp into AI consulting, and for OAI, a pipeline of new potential Business customers.

QUICK HITS

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ Vicky built a marketing tracker that fills itself in

Today’s workflow comes from reader Vicky DiMichele:

“I used to spend a lot of time pulling marketing numbers from Google Analytics, OpenAI Ads, Google Ads, Meta, email, and other sources. Now I have a Google Sheet that updates itself every week. It's built for anyone who tracks marketing across several platforms and wants the reporting done automatically.

I created a sheet in my Google Drive to serve as my marketing tracker. I linked Metricool to track my social accounts. My email program isn't linked yet, so for now I take screenshots of my weekly email reports and add them to the chat.

The workflow runs weekly and pulls in my data automatically. The only step I do myself is screenshotting the weekly email reports, and the tasks add that information to the sheet as well. The result is a marketing tracker that fills itself in for weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly tracking, so I spend far less time on data collection.”

  • 🚢 Claude Ship - Claude agents that review code and approve routine fixes

Virginia and Oregon sued SpaceX over Grok, saying Elon Musk's AI app let users create and spread explicit deepfakes of real people, including children.

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 8,176 new readers. Few fields have changed more under AI this past year than math. Now, a single Anthropic mathematician and Claude may have solved a problem even the top minds thought was years, if not decades, away.

Levent Alpöge says they just proved the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old prime-number puzzle that carries a $1M Millennium Prize and has long been seen as math's most famous open problem. As with AI's other big math wins, not everyone is thrilled.

In today’s AI rundown:

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

ANTHROPIC, AI, & MATHEMATICS

🧮 Claude helps solve math's biggest open problem

Image source: Claude / The Rundown

The Rundown: Anthropic’s Levent Alpöge used Claude to crack the Riemann hypothesis, the 167-year-old question often ranked as math's biggest unsolved problem, after ~6 weeks of work, and checkers say it holds up, even as no human fully gets it yet.

The details:

  • First posed in 1859, the problem asks whether prime numbers follow a predictable pattern, and the Clay Institute put a $1M “Millennium” prize on solving it in 2000.

  • Alpöge shared the proof only as 17M lines of machine-checkable math, writing that Claude “flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.”

  • The groups behind Lean, the computer language used for verification, certified it on Saturday, saying they have “full confidence” that Alpöge’s proof is correct.

  • The Association for Human Mathematics criticized the proof as “little more than publicity” for AI labs, saying no human could reasonably understand it.

  • A rival proof from Alessandro Masullo surfaced hours later, reportedly made without AI over nearly 12 years, though others quickly flagged problems in it.

Why it matters: The Riemann hypothesis was a problem top mathematicians expected to take decades of new theory to solve, and Alpöge and Claude just blew past those estimates. This proof may not change daily life, but once that speed of progress spreads to fields like biology and drug design, the practical payoff will really start to show up.

THE RUNDOWN ROUNDTABLE

💡 The Rundown Roundtable: Our AI use cases

The Rundown: The Rundown Roundtable is a weekly feature where we poll members of The Rundown staff about how we use AI in our work and daily lives.

Kenny, Head of Sales: After a good discovery call, my proposal used to take so long that the buyer's urgency faded and the details got fuzzy. This workflow fixes that. I record the call using Granola, have Claude pull out the buyer's own ask, and draft the proposal from that instead of from a rate card.

Proposals built from the buyer's own words close faster than generic decks, and offering a smaller “yes” option turns “too expensive” into “let's test it.”

Result: a proposal drafted in about 10 minutes, sent while the buyer is still engaged, with the deal history logged in the CRM.

Shubham, Editor: My investments sit across several platforms, so I use Claude to bring them into one unified dashboard. Instead of logging in to each app, I can see every mutual fund and stock I hold in one place, along with what goes into each one every month and how often.

Live holdings and company fundamentals come in through MCP connectors, so the numbers match my broker, and holdings from my other platforms appear in the same view. Claude fetches a short summary of each position and updates it daily. It sets up reminders for each SIP date, the 10% step-up every April, other amount changes, and when tax is payable.

The result is one accurate view with no logging in to each app and no spreadsheet to update by hand. Claude does the fetching, organizing, and reminding, and I make the decisions.

AI TRAINING

🧠 Test Gemini 4 Neon on finding billing errors

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll put Google’s new Gemini 4 Neon to work on an everyday job: reading a year of electricity bills against your bank’s payment history to find why the bill jumped and what was billed wrong, then drafting the dispute email.

Step-by-step:

  1. Download a year of electricity bills as PDFs and your bank’s payment history as a CSV. Delete every bank row that isn’t a payment to the utility

  2. Start a temporary chat in the Gemini app, choose Deeper analysis (4 Neon) from the model menu, and set Thinking level to High

  3. Attach both files and ask for a month-by-month table of usage, rate, and total, plus which month jumped and why

  4. Ask where each problem appears in the files: the PDF page and line, or the bank row. Check two or three of those spots yourself before you rely on them

  5. Ask for a short dispute email with every date and amount. Check it against the files, then send it to the utility

Pro tip: Ask for the evidence before you act on an answer. A model that names the page, line, or row is easy to check, and only takes a minute.

AI RESEARCH

📋 OpenAI opens its private AI scorecard to rivals

Image source: OpenAI

The Rundown: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki just published the internal scores the company uses to track the raw intelligence of its AI since GPT-3.5, asking rival labs to agree on shared limits they'd hold until tools for monitoring AI catch up.

The details:

  • The metric, log-perplexity, measures how well an AI predicts the next token; lower scores indicate better predictions, and Pachocki says it tracks with AI's big jumps.

  • Pachocki tied OpenAI's biggest new skills in cybersecurity and math to scores below 0.8, down from about 0.99 for the model behind the original ChatGPT.

  • OAI also revealed an unreleased internal model at ~0.73, with Pachocki saying they should “expect further transformative capabilities” in the 0.68–0.7 range.

  • Sam Altman called the post “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while,” saying agreeing on common limits “would be very wise.”

Why it matters: This post packs in three reveals: another call for industry-wide “common limits” on progress, a first look at where OpenAI's next internal model stands, and a marker for where the next big jump in capabilities should land. Similar to METR's report on Anthropic, the data is showing that acceleration curves aren't slowing down.
